summary: Sharada Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Jai Hind College, IIT Bombay, SOAS University of London, and University College London, and has been a professor at the National Institute of Advanced Studies since 2001.

Sharon J. Roe works in religious studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

Sharon Salzberg is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner and scholar. She studied at the University at Buffalo and trained under teachers including Anagarika Munindra, S. N. Goenka, Dipa Ma, Sayadaw U Pandita, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, co-founding IMS and BCBS.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta (1911–1964) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (earning an MA and PhD), where he served as a lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and UCLA under Gregory Schopen (PhD 2006). He has served as an associate professor at McMaster University and research fellow at IIBS.

Shechen Gyaltsab (1871–1926) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous masters, including Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche is a Tibetan Buddhist teacher active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under his spiritual teacher, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held an academic post at Cornell University from circa 1978 to 1998 before becoming a professor at Harvard University around 1998.

Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Ying-Kuang Chu, and Yui Chi Lau, founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies Association in North America, and held posts at Renmin University and Tsinghua University.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University (2005–2021), and served as general editor of the Clay Sanskrit Library.

Sheng Yen (1931–2009) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University, founded Dharma Drum Mountain and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and taught at Shandao Temple and National Cheng Kung University.

Shenghai Li works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., and held fellowships at Harvard University (2013–2015) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2015–2016).

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, while also training under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under masters including Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, taught at Dzogchen Monastery, and became the first khenpo of the shedra at Dzongsar Monastery.

Sherab Chomphel works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a BA at the College for Higher Tibetan Studies, an MA at Banaras Hindu University, and an MTS at Harvard University (2022–2025).

Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries, co-founded and served as president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953–1966), and was dean of the Buddhist Academy of China.

Sherry B. Ortner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Bryn Mawr College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan, and held faculty positions at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and UCLA.
Sherry Chayat works in the field of Buddhist studies. She completed her studies at Vassar College from circa 1961 to 1965 and trained under traditional teacher Eido Shimano from circa 1967 to 1998.
Shesh Dev Pandey is an Indology scholar who completed his Shastri degree at Banaras Hindu University between 2020 and 2023, where he was recorded as a student in 2020.

Shi Hu (1891–1962) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and history. He studied at Cornell University and Columbia University under John Dewey, later serving on the faculty at Peking University (ca. 1917–1948) and as president of Academia Sinica (1958–1962).
